title: A flat Noetherian model with a prescribed algebra element
statement: Let $A\to B$ be a flat [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map] finitely presented [def-weil-pbc-finitely-presented-algebra] homomorphism of commutative rings, and let $a\in B$. There exist a subring $A_0\subseteq A$ containing the image of $\mathbf Z$ and generated by finitely many elements as a $\mathbf Z$-algebra, a flat finitely presented $A_0$-algebra $B_0$, an element $a_0\in B_0$, and an $A$-algebra isomorphism $e:A\otimes_{A_0}B_0\xrightarrow{\sim}B$ with $e(1\otimes a_0)=a$ [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. Both $A_0$ and $B_0$ are Noetherian rings [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring].

source.place: Tag 056Y, label lemma-slice-given-element, proof, second paragraph: flat Noetherian approximation with descent of the chosen section (old steps 3–5).

proof.text: Choose a presentation $B\cong A[x_1,\ldots,x_n]/(f_1,\ldots,f_m)$ and a polynomial $g\in A[x_1,\ldots,x_n]$ representing $a$. Let $R\subseteq A$ be the subring generated by the image of $\mathbf Z$ and all coefficients of the finitely many $f_j$ and of $g$. These are finite sets. Write $f_{j,R},g_R$ for the same polynomials over $R$, and put $C=R[x_1,\ldots,x_n]/(f_{1,R},\ldots,f_{m,R})$. This is finitely presented by the cited definition. There is an $A$-algebra isomorphism $e_R:A\otimes_R C\to B$ sending $u\otimes[P]$ to $u[P]$. Indeed the reverse map sends the class of each $x_i$ to $1\otimes[x_i]$ and each coefficient $u$ to $u\otimes1$; each $f_j$ goes to $1\otimes[f_{j,R}]=0$ by tensor balancing, so it factors through the displayed quotient. The two composites fix coefficients and variables, which generate the polynomial quotients; on the tensor product they fix every $u\otimes[P]$ by bilinearity. Thus they are inverses. In particular $e_R(1\otimes[g_R])=a$.

source.place: Tag 00F3 (definition-finite-type), finite presentations; Tag 00R0 (lemma-limit-finite-presentation), explicit coefficient construction; Tag 00CX (lemma-tensor-product), universal property.

proof.text: Let $I$ be the set of subrings $T\subseteq A$ generated by finitely many elements over the image of $\mathbf Z$ and containing $R$, ordered by inclusion. It is nonempty, with least element $R$, and directed: the subring generated by the union of two finite generating sets contains both. Its union is $A$, since any $u\in A$ lies in the subring generated by $R$ and $u$. The inclusions exhibit $A$ as the ring colimit of this diagram: compatible ring maps from the $T$ to any commutative ring define a unique map on their union, and directedness verifies preservation of addition and multiplication by putting any two elements in a common $T$. This checks the precise colimit hypothesis needed below.

source.place: Tag 00R0 (lemma-limit-finite-presentation), finitely generated coefficient subrings; Tag 02JO (lemma-flat-finite-presentation-limit-flat), proof of (2), directed base-ring system.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-colimit-flat-ring-map] to this directed system, with its chosen initial index $R$, initial lower algebra $R$ itself, initial upper algebra $C$, and initial map $R\to C$. This map is finitely presented by step 1. At the limit the lower algebra $A\otimes_R R$ identifies with $A$ by $u\otimes r\mapsto ur$ with inverse $u\mapsto u\otimes1$; the upper algebra identifies with $B$ by $e_R$. The limit map is therefore the given flat map $A\to B$. The cited theorem supplies an index $A_0\in I$ such that $A_0\to B_0=A_0\otimes_R C$ is flat, using the identical lower-algebra identification $A_0\otimes_R R\cong A_0$. All hypotheses are now checked: the index set is directed, the base-ring colimit is $A$, the two initial algebras are commutative $R$-algebras, the initial map is finitely presented, and the limit map is flat.

source.place: Tag 02JO (lemma-flat-finite-presentation-limit-flat), part (3), specialized to the algebra and its rank-one module; equivalently the ring-map form cited in Tag 04AI.

proof.text: The map $A_0\to B_0$ is finitely presented by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-presentation-base-change-composition](1) applied to $R\to C$. Define $a_0=1\otimes[g_R]\in B_0$. The tensor universal property gives inverse $A$-algebra maps $A\otimes_{A_0}(A_0\otimes_R C)\leftrightarrows A\otimes_R C$ by $u\otimes(v\otimes c)\mapsto uv\otimes c$ and $u\otimes c\mapsto u\otimes(1\otimes c)$. Balancing verifies well-definedness, and the two composites are identities on pure tensors. Compose the first map with $e_R$ to obtain $e:A\otimes_{A_0}B_0\cong B$. Its value at $1\otimes a_0$ is $e_R(1\otimes[g_R])=a$. By its membership in $I$, $A_0$ is a subring of $A$ containing the integer image and is generated by finitely many elements over it.

source.place: Tag 05G5 (lemma-base-change-finiteness), part (4); Tag 00CX (lemma-tensor-product), iterated scalar extension; Tag 056Y (lemma-slice-given-element), second proof paragraph, descent of the specified element.

proof.text: The ring $\mathbf Z$ is Noetherian: a nonzero ideal is generated by its least positive element, since Euclidean division leaves a smaller nonnegative remainder in the ideal; the zero ideal has the empty generating set. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-noetherian] to the finitely generated $\mathbf Z$-algebra $A_0$ to conclude that $A_0$ is Noetherian. Apply it again to $A_0\to B_0$: its finite presentation from step 4 gives finitely many algebra generators by discarding the finiteness condition on the relations. Thus $B_0$ is Noetherian as well. Together with steps 3 and 4 these are all required clauses.
